title: Students march to the Houet High Commissioner over SOTRACO buses
location: Bobo-Dioulasso, Houet Province; march to the High Commissioner's office
organizer: Students/pupils who used SOTRACO; named organization not established
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Sources identify students/pupils and describe a march, but no numeric or clear qualitative attendance evidence establishes 50 simultaneous participants.

start_date.summary: La Tribune search extract and 3TV description date the march to 18 Nov 2024; L'Express later states a march occurred on 18 Nov. The exact La Tribune body was blocked; S002 body and snippets support date.

occurrence.summary: Search-only La Tribune/3TV descriptions and NetAfrique partial body describe students marching to the Houet High Commissioner; L'Express refers to the 18 Nov march.

location.summary: Bobo-Dioulasso; official recipient was the High Commissioner of Houet, per source descriptions.

participants.summary: Sources say students/pupils; no headcount or clear crowd-size description.

demands.summary: Students objected to poor bus condition, insufficient buses, overcrowding and unreliable schedules. The categories supplied by the project do not map cleanly to this public transport demand; no category coded.

state_target.summary: The march was directed to the provincial High Commissioner and described as an appeal to local authorities; NetAfrique body says they marched there to present their claims.

state_response.summary: Search snippet says the High Commissioner received the demonstrators and promised discussions; NetAfrique body reports the official cited buses awaiting repair. Whether this was an accommodation or policy response is unresolved.

violence.summary: No event-specific protester violence evidence obtained; coded unknown.

notes: Distinct public march to a state official on 18 Nov, before the 20 Nov fatal-bus-incident protest. Do not merge automatically: shared transport grievance, but separate dates and immediate triggers. Private service complaint becomes relevant here because students publicly appealed to a state authority. No attendance number; do not infer >=50 from plural 'students'. Companies' statements about repairs/capital are not themselves state action.
open_questions: Was there a simultaneous attendance count or sufficiently clear scale description?
Did the High Commissioner enact any remedy or only promise discussions?
Are the 18 and 20 Nov events linked to one continuous movement or separate gatherings?
Do adjacent-month sources show continuation beyond Nov?

title: Students protest in Bobo-Dioulasso after a fatal SOTRACO bus incident
location: Place Tiéfo Amoro/SOTRACO station area, Bobo-Dioulasso
organizer: Students and pupils; FESCI-BF/student representatives quoted; formal organizer unclear
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. LeFaso and L'Express describe students/pupils and LeFaso quotes 'strong mobilization' without quantifying or clearly establishing at least 50 simultaneous participants.

start_date.summary: Both opened local reports date the protest to Wednesday 20 Nov 2024.

occurrence.summary: LeFaso and L'Express body reads report students/pupils protesting in Bobo after a fatal accidental bus incident; Wakat Séra is search-only after exact URL returned 403.

location.summary: LeFaso identifies Place Tiéfo Amoro near the SOTRACO station; L'Express also locates related incident in Bobo-Dioulasso sector 24.

participants.summary: Reports identify students/pupils; no numerical estimate. 'Forte mobilisation' in a quoted statement is not sufficiently clear for the 50-person threshold.

demands.summary: Students sought justice/accountability, safer bus conditions and monthly technical inspections, urging authorities to act; taxonomy lacks a clear public-transport-safety category, so no category coded.

state_target.summary: Students explicitly appealed to authorities to inspect buses and address the issue; this supports domestic state/policy target, despite the transport company's role.

state_response.summary: An official search result title reports a government delegation visited the family and students after the death. The page body timed out, and the snippet does not establish that the visit responded to the protest; no response field is upgraded.

protester_violence.summary: Reports describe a fatal accidental bus event before the protest; no evidence attributes the death to state force or reports protester violence. Protester violence remains unknown.

notes: Keep separate from 18 Nov candidate unless further evidence establishes continuity. The student's fatality is described as accidental and involving a SOTRACO bus; it is not coded as state killing. LeFaso and L'Express quote overlapping student representatives; treat source independence as unresolved rather than two independent count confirmations.
open_questions: Is there a headcount or independent contemporaneous estimate establishing at least 50 simultaneously present?
Was the ministry delegation visit a response to the protest or to the accidental death?
Were there subsequent gatherings after 20 Nov, or did the event end that day?
